talking_points.headline: External AI-agent access raises authorization and liability questions
talking_points.context_html: The KSNV report describes consumer hesitation, survey findings and US banks blocking some third-party agents that use customer credentials. For banking operations, a key control question is whether customers can authorize constrained agent actions without sharing passwords, and how disputed or mistaken actions would be handled. The evidence combines one local news report, survey results and expert commentary, so it should not be treated as a measure of APAC customer adoption or risk.

talking_points.headline: Survey points to Asian interest in collecting as a wealth conversation
talking_points.context_html: HSBC Private Bank’s report says surveyed wealthy entrepreneurs in mainland China, Singapore and India show substantial fine-wine collecting, with many Singapore respondents expecting to spend more for enjoyment. For wealth delivery, this may inform client conversations and specialist-content needs, while any service decision would depend on validated client demand and the suitability of the offering. The findings are survey-based and do not demonstrate a change in client behaviour beyond the reported responses.

talking_points.headline: Screen privacy and transaction authority are separate control questions
talking_points.context_html: Signal says operating-system agents may read displayed app content and is adding platform-specific screen protections, while acknowledging residual access paths. For wealth and banking delivery, a useful design question is whether controls cover only visible information or also data access, delegated permissions and actions; the article describes one app’s measures, not a tested banking standard.

AI & Technology.title: Signal joins United Airlines, banks in limiting AI agents over customer risks - CNBC
AI & Technology.summary: Signal says it will block screenshots in its iOS app and enable screen security on Android when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen, citing the possibility that agents could capture app data beyond its control. It also says these measures do not close every access route, including data already stored on a device. The report notes that banks including JPMorgan Chase and OCBC restrict some third-party agent access; for banking change execution, the distinction between screen access, stored data and transaction authority is a practical control-design issue, not evidence of a common industry standard.

AI & Technology.title: Consumers weigh risks as banks warn AI agent mistakes could be customers’ liability
AI & Technology.summary: A KSNV report cites an ABA survey in which 27% of respondents said they were likely to let an AI agent autonomously manage their bank accounts in the next 12 months, while 20% said an agent had already requested login credentials or a card number. The report also describes consumer concerns, expert warnings about excessive permissions and manipulation, and several US banks blocking external agents from logging in with customer credentials. For banking delivery, the coverage underlines the need to distinguish authorized access from credential sharing and to define liability and escalation controls; the survey and expert views do not establish adoption or risk rates across markets.

AI & Technology.title: SFF 2026 Hackcelerator Winner LinqAlpha Names New Chief Product Officer
AI & Technology.summary: AI investment-research firm LinqAlpha appointed Jae Leeholland as chief product officer to lead global product strategy and platform development for institutional investors. The company previously launched an AI Lab and raised US$22 million in Series A funding, according to the article. The appointment is a limited competitor signal on AI product leadership; the report does not establish product outcomes or adoption by financial institutions.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Asia’s wealthy are leading the world in fine wine collecting – HSBC Private Bank - Fund Selector Asia
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: HSBC Private Bank and Justerini & Brooks published a survey-based report on fine wine and rare whisky collecting, drawing on more than 3,000 HNW and UHNW entrepreneurs. It says 54% of mainland China respondents collect fine wine, compared with 36% in Singapore and India, and 43% of Singapore respondents expect to spend more on their collections for enjoyment over the next 12 months. The findings offer public evidence of collecting interests among surveyed wealthy clients in Asia, but they do not establish broader market demand or specify any change to HSBC’s wealth services.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Fine Wine, Whisky Buyers Widen Horizons For Tasty Results – HSBC - Wealth Briefing
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: HSBC Private Bank and Justerini & Brooks published the A Taste for Time report on fine-wine and rare-whisky collecting, based on a survey of more than 3,000 HNW and UHNW entrepreneurs. The article repeats previously reported survey findings on collecting and expected spending, and adds that Scotland exports 43 bottles of whisky every second to more than 160 markets. The coverage reinforces the public profile of passion assets in wealth discussions, but survey responses do not establish broader market demand or a change to HSBC services.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: UBP hires senior wealth planner in HK - Fund Selector Asia
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: UBP appointed Don Lai as senior wealth planner in Hong Kong, effective 23 November 2026, to support its North Asia wealth-planning business. The article says Lai previously held wealth-planning roles at UBS and DBS and earlier roles at Standard Chartered and HSBC. The hire is competitor context for Hong Kong wealth-planning capacity; the report provides no detail on client volumes or changes to service delivery.

Regulatory & Markets.title: ECB and Sveriges Riksbank conclude agreement for Sweden to join T2
Regulatory & Markets.summary: The ECB and Sveriges Riksbank signed an agreement for Sweden to join T2 for large-value payments in Swedish kronor, with migration targeted for February 2030. The move would replace Sweden’s national settlement platform with shared European infrastructure while retaining settlement in central bank money. For banking operations, the long lead time makes migration planning and coordination with market participants relevant, but the announcement gives no detailed implementation plan or immediate service change.
